newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse trade at record high close.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse trade at record high close.

text.p: Germany's DAX index, which measures trade in 30 blue-chip German shares, closed bourse dealings on Tuesday at an all-time record closing high after Wall Street's strength overnight, a firmer dollar and bond gains.
The DAX closed up 34.57 points, or 1.28 percent, at 2,728.45, after briefly touching 2,728.64.
The Dow Jones Industrial index ended Monday's trade on Wall Street at 6,010 points, the first close above the 6,000-point level, boosting all the European markets.
The stronger U.S. dollar, which eyed the 1.54 mark level, was also a boost for export-oriented German firms.
The DAX had spent the last few trading days consolidating just below the 2,700 point level, after record highs were posted early last week, but had been widely expected to make another upward run.
"Everything is really positive," said one trader, "It's not just the Dow, people are generally positive on the DAX and we've been consolidating for a few days."

Dealers said Western European car registration figures out after the end of trade on Monday had given a boost to auto stocks, which, as major exporters, were also boosted by the strength of the dollar.

Car manufacturer Daimler Benz AG was the DAX's biggest climber, adding over three percent after the news to add 2.73 marks to end bourse trade at 86.65 marks, touching a year high of 86.80 during the day.

Auto maker BMW AG also climbed, ending bourse trade up 23.50 marks at 904 marks. The company announced on Tuesday that its UK Rover group was planning investment in a new vehicle at its Land Rover plant.
Dealers said positive nine-month sales figures from Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG was supporting the German chemicals sector.

Among the medium-sized stocks, pharmaceutical group Gehe AG gained 2.75 to touch a bourse year high of 110.50 after it said it would sell its pharmaceutical production units for around 1.2 billion marks.
The group then slipped back on profit taking to end floor trade down 0.75 at 107 marks.
Troubled German engineering group Deutsch Babcock AG, which slipped to a year low on Monday, recovered some ground to end floor dealings up 3.60 marks at 51.00.
